f.title: Definition: abuse of a medicinal product
f.statement: Definition (determines reportable use outside the marketing authorisation): abuse of a medicinal product is persistent or sporadic, intentional excessive use of medicinal products which is accompanied by harmful physical or psychological effects.
f.clause: Annex I - Abuse of a medicinal product

rows.quote: Persistent or sporadic, intentional excessive use of medicinal products which is accompanied by harmful physical or psychological effects [DIR 2001/83/EC Art 1(16)].
rows.location: Annex I - Abuse of a medicinal product
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Legal definition (DIR Art 1(16)) quoted exactly. Currency: EMA GVP page (checked 2026-11-10) lists Annex I Rev. 5 (EMA/876333/2011, effective 06/08/2024), matching this text; no duplicate committed curation.

f.title: Definition: adverse event in a clinical trial
f.statement: Definition: in the context of a clinical trial, an adverse event is any untoward medical occurrence in a subject to whom a medicinal product is administered and which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment.

rows.quote: In the context of a clinical trial: Any untoward medical occurrence in a subject to whom a medicinal product is administered and which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment [Reg (EU) No 536/2014 Art 2(2)(32)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). CTR definition (Reg 536/2014 Art 2(2)(32)); sponsor actor inferred.

f.title: Definition: adverse event outside a clinical trial
f.statement: Definition: in pharmacovigilance outside a clinical trial, an adverse event is any untoward medical occurrence in a patient to whom a medicinal product is administered which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment; it can be any unfavourable and unintended sign, symptom or disease temporally associated with use, whether or not considered related.

rows.quote: In the context of pharmacovigilance and outside a clinical trial: Any untoward medical occurrence in a patient to whom a medicinal product is administered and which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment (based on ICH-E2D Guideline, see GVP Annex IV). An adverse event can therefore be any unfavourable and unintended sign (e.g. an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a medicinal product, whether or not considered related to this medicinal product (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D Guideline).
rows.review_note: Review: Level Recommended confirmed (definition based on ICH-E2D, no legal citation). Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). ICH-E2D-based definition, Recommended correct.

f.title: Definition: adverse reaction (noxious and unintended response)
f.statement: Definition: an adverse reaction is a response to a medicinal product which is noxious and unintended.

rows.quote: A response to a medicinal product which is noxious and unintended [DIR 2001/83/EC Art 1(11)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Legal definition (DIR Art 1(11)) quoted exactly.

f.title: Treat all spontaneous reports as suspected adverse reactions unless the primary source excludes causality
f.statement: For regulatory reporting purposes, a spontaneously reported event meets the adverse reaction definition even if the relationship is unknown or unstated by the primary source; all spontaneous reports notified by healthcare professionals or consumers are considered suspected adverse reactions unless the primary source specifically states that the event is unrelated or that a causal relationship can be excluded.
f.exceptions: Not where the primary source specifically states the event is unrelated or a causal relationship can be excluded.

rows.quote: For regulatory reporting purposes, if an event is spontaneously reported, even if the relationship is unknown or unstated by the by healthcare professional or consumer as primary source, it meets the definition of an adverse reaction (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D). Therefore all spontaneous reports notified by healthcare professionals or consumers are considered suspected adverse reactions, since they convey the Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – Annex I (Rev 5) EMA/876333/2011 Rev 5 of 26 July 2024 Page 6/32  suspicions of the primary sources, unless the primary source specifically state that they believe the event to be unrelated or that a causal relationship can be excluded.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Quote contains page-header text; reporting convention paraphrased; Recommended correct (no legal citation).

f.title: Adverse reactions include use within or outside the marketing authorisation and occupational exposure
f.statement: Adverse reactions may arise from use of the product within or outside the terms of the marketing authorisation or from occupational exposure.

rows.quote: Adverse reactions may arise from use of the product within or outside the terms of the marketing authorisation or from occupational exposure [DIR 2001/83/EC Art 101(1)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'may arise' is a scope statement, not a duty; Mandatory kept only because DIR Art 101(1) is cited - judgement call on level. Actor inferred.

f.title: Definition: consumer as reporter
f.statement: Definition: for reporting suspected adverse reactions, a consumer is a person who is not a healthcare professional, such as a patient, lawyer, friend or relative of a patient, or carer.

rows.quote: For the purpose of reporting cases of suspected adverse reactions, a person who is not a healthcare professional such as a patient, lawyer, friend or relative of a patient (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D Guideline) or carer.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party).

f.title: Definition: emerging safety issue requiring urgent authority attention
f.statement: Definition: an emerging safety issue is a safety issue considered by a MAH to require urgent attention by the competent authority because of the potential major impact on the risk-benefit balance and/or on patients' or public health and the potential need for prompt regulatory action and communication; examples include major safety issues from ongoing or newly completed studies, from spontaneous reporting or literature, and major safety-related regulatory actions outside the EU.

rows.quote: A safety issue considered by a marketing authorisation holder to require urgent attention by the competent authority because of the potential major impact on the risk-benefit balance of the medicinal product and/or on patients’ or public health and the potential need for prompt regulatory action and communication to patients and healthcare professionals. Examples include: • major safety issues identified in the context of ongoing or newly completed studies, e.g. an unexpectedly increased rate of fatal or life-threatening adverse events; • major safety issues identified through the spontaneous reporting system or publications in the scientific literature, which may lead to considering a contraindication, a restriction of use of a medicinal product or its withdrawal from the market; • major safety-related regulatory actions outside the EU, e.g. a restriction of use of a medicinal product or its suspension.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Examples list summarised in the statement.

f.title: Definition: EU (Union) reference date
f.statement: Definition: the EU reference date is, for products with the same active substance or combination, the date of the first marketing authorisation in the EU of a product containing it, or if this cannot be ascertained, the earliest known marketing authorisation date.

rows.quote: For medicinal products containing the same active substance or the same combination of active substances, the date of the first marketing authorisation in the EU of a medicinal product containing that active substance or that combination of active substances; or if this date cannot be ascertained, the earliest of the known dates of the marketing authorisations for a medicinal product containing that active substance or that combination of active substances [DIR 2001/83/EC Art 107c(5)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Legal definition (DIR Art 107c(5)) quoted exactly.

f.title: Definition: healthcare professional as reporter; excludes MAH and authority employees
f.statement: Definition: in reporting suspected adverse reactions, a healthcare professional is a medically qualified person such as a physician, dentist, pharmacist, nurse or coroner, or as otherwise specified by local regulations; the term does not include those qualified as healthcare professionals who work as employees of a MAH or competent authority.

rows.quote: In the context of reporting suspected adverse reactions: Medically qualified persons, such as physicians, dentists, pharmacists, nurses and coroners, or as otherwise specified by local regulations (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D Guideline). In the context of risk minimisation: A person providing professional healthcare8 to individual patients, and also a healthcare professional representative or organisation (including learned societies and clinical guideline working groups) as target populations of risk minimisation measures. The term healthcare professional does not include those who are qualified as a healthcare professional but work as employees of a marketing authorisation holder or a competent authority.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Risk-minimisation sense of HCP in the quote is not carried into the statement (statement limited to the reporting sense plus the exclusion).

f.title: Consider risks likely to be in contraindications or warnings as important
f.statement: What constitutes an important identified or potential risk depends on several factors, including the impact on the individual, the seriousness of the risk and the impact on public health; normally, any risk that is likely to be included in the contraindications or warnings and precautions section of the product information should be considered important.
f.clause: Annex I - Important identified risk and Important potential risk

rows.quote: What constitutes an important risk will depend upon several factors, including the impact on the individual, the seriousness of the risk and the impact on public health. Normally, any risk that is likely to be included in the contraindications or warnings and precautions section of the product information should be considered important
rows.location: Annex I - Important identified risk and Important potential risk
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Statement trimmed to the quote: the opening 'could impact the risk-benefit balance or have public health implications' was not in the quote. 'should be considered important' read as Recommended; actor inferred.

f.title: Determine the IBD; if unknown, use published listings or propose one for agreement
f.statement: The IBD is the date of the first marketing authorisation for any product containing the active substance granted to any company in any country. If a MAH has no information on the actual IBD, it should first refer to publicly available birth date listings; if the product is not listed, it should propose to the regulatory authority a birth date based on the earliest known marketing authorisation of the substance and obtain the authority's agreement.

rows.quote: The date of the first marketing authorisation for any product containing the active substance granted to any company in any country in the world (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2C(R2) Guideline). If a marketing authorisation holder has no information on the actual IBD for a product, it should first refer to listings of birth dates that some regions develop and make publicly available. If the product is not included in any listing, it should propose to the regulatory authority a birth date that is based on the earliest known marketing authorisation of the substance and then obtain the regulatory authority’s agreement (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2C(R2) Q&A).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Recommended (should) correct; MAH named in the quote; definition part from ICH-E2C(R2). Two 'should' steps merged with the definition.

f.title: Definition: medication error; distinguish from intentional overdose, off-label use, misuse and abuse
f.statement: Definition: a medication error is an unintended failure in the drug treatment process that leads to, or has the potential to lead to, harm to the patient; it refers to human or process mediated failures, not lack of efficacy. Intentional overdose, off-label use, misuse and abuse should be clearly distinguished from medication errors.

rows.quote: An unintended failure in the drug treatment process that leads to, or has the potential to lead to, harm to the patient (see EMA-PRAC Good Practice Guide on Recording, Coding, Reporting and Assessment of Medication Errors, 23 October 2015). A failure in the drug treatment process does not refer to lack of efficacy of the drug, rather to human or process mediated failures. Intentional overdose, off-label use, misuse and abuse should be clearly distinguished from medication errors
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). 'should be clearly distinguished' read as Recommended.

f.title: Minimum criteria for a reportable case and for expedited ICSRs
f.statement: For reporting suspected adverse reactions, the minimum data elements for a case are an identifiable reporter, an identifiable patient, an adverse reaction and a suspect medicinal product. In expedited reporting, the ICSR shall include at least an identifiable reporter, an identifiable patient, one suspected adverse reaction and the medicinal product(s) concerned.
f.clause: Annex I - Minimum criteria for reporting

rows.quote: For the purpose of reporting cases of suspected adverse reactions, the minimum data elements for a case are: an identifiable reporter, an identifiable patient, an adverse reaction and a suspect medicinal product (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D Guideline). In the case of expedited reporting, the individual case safety report shall include at least an identifiable reporter, an identifiable patient, one suspected adverse reaction and the medicinal product(s) concerned [IR 520/2012 Art 28(1)].
rows.location: Annex I - Minimum criteria for reporting
rows.review_note: Review: Level Mandatory confirmed because the second sentence cites IR 520/2012 Art 28(1); the first sentence (ICH-E2D minimum case) is guidance. Double-check: Mandatory supported by the shall in IR 520/2012 Art 28(1) for the second sentence; first sentence is ICH-E2D guidance merged into the same row; actor inferred.

f.title: Definition: misuse and misuse for illegal purposes
f.statement: Definition: misuse is intentional and inappropriate use not in accordance with the terms of the marketing authorisation; misuse for illegal purposes additionally implies an intention to cause an effect in another person, including sale for recreational purposes and use to facilitate assault.
f.clause: Annex I - Misuse of a medicinal product

rows.quote: Situations where a medicinal product is intentionally and inappropriately used not in accordance with the terms of the marketing authorisation. See also Misuse of a medicinal product for illegal purposes Misuse of a medicinal product for illegal purposes Misuse for illegal purposes is misuse with the additional connotation of an intention of misusing the medicinal product to cause an effect in another person. This includes, amongst others: the sale, to other people, of medicines for recreational purposes and use of a medicinal product to facilitate assault.
rows.location: Annex I - Misuse of a medicinal product
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Quote contains the repeated heading 'Misuse of a medicinal product for illegal purposes' (layout artefact) and merges two definitions.

f.title: Definition: non-interventional study (outside the scope of the Clinical Trials Regulation)
f.statement: Definition: a non-interventional study is a clinical study other than a clinical trial; non-interventional studies do not fall within the scope of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014.

rows.quote: A clinical study other than a clinical trial [Reg (EU) No 536/2014 Art 2(2)(4)]. Non-interventional studies do not fall in the scope of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 [Reg (EU) No 536/2014 Art 1].
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Definition cites Reg (EU) No 536/2014 and decides whether CTR or post-authorisation reporting rules apply -> Mandatory. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Definition cites Reg 536/2014 Art 2(2)(4) and Art 1; Mandatory follows the legal citation.

f.title: Definition: occupational exposure (excludes manufacturing exposure)
f.statement: Definition: for reporting suspected adverse reactions, occupational exposure is exposure to a medicinal product as a result of one's professional or non-professional occupation; it does not include exposure to an ingredient during manufacturing before release as finished product.
f.clause: Annex I - Occupational exposure to a medicinal product

rows.quote: For the purpose of reporting cases of suspected adverse reactions, an exposure to a medicinal product as a result of one’s professional or non-professional occupation. It does not include the exposure to one of the ingredients during the manufacturing process before the release as finished product.
rows.location: Annex I - Occupational exposure to a medicinal product
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party).

f.title: Definition: off-label use
f.statement: Definition: off-label use is the intentional use of a medicinal product for a medical purpose not in accordance with the terms of the marketing authorisation, e.g. a different indication, patient group, route or method of administration or posology.

rows.quote: Situations where a medicinal product is intentionally used for a medical purpose not in accordance with the terms of the marketing authorisation. Examples include the intentional use of a product in situations other than the ones described in the authorised product information, such as a different indication in terms of medical condition, a different group of patients (e.g. a different age group), a different route or method of administration or a different posology.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Examples summarised.

f.title: Definition: overdose, applying clinical judgement
f.statement: Definition: overdose is administration of a quantity of a medicinal product, per administration or cumulatively, above the maximum recommended dose according to the authorised product information; clinical judgement should always be applied.

rows.quote: Administration of a quantity of a medicinal product given per administration or cumulatively which is above the maximum recommended dose according to the authorised product information. When applying this definition, clinical judgement should always be applied.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). 'clinical judgement should always be applied' gives the Recommended level.

f.title: Definition: post-authorisation safety study (PASS)
f.statement: Definition: a post-authorisation safety study is any study relating to an authorised medicinal product conducted with the aim of identifying, characterising or quantifying a safety hazard, confirming the safety profile of the medicinal product, or of measuring the effectiveness of risk management measures.

rows.quote: Any study relating to an authorised medicinal product conducted with the aim of identifying, characterising or quantifying a safety hazard, confirming the safety profile of the medicinal product, or of measuring the effectiveness of risk management measures [DIR 2001/83/EC Art 1(15)].
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Definition cites the Directive and determines when PASS obligations (protocol, reporting) apply -> Mandatory. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Legal definition (DIR Art 1(15)) quoted exactly.

f.title: Definition: reference safety information for PBRERs
f.statement: Definition: in PBRERs, the reference safety information is all relevant safety information in the MAH's reference product information (e.g. the company core data sheet) which the MAH requires to be listed in all countries where it markets the product, except where the local authority requires a modification; where the reference product information is the CCDS, the RSI is the CCSI.

rows.quote: In periodic benefit-risk evaluation reports for medicinal products, all relevant safety information contained in the reference product information (e.g. the company core data sheet) prepared by the marketing authorisation holder and which the marketing authorisation holder requires to be listed in all countries where it markets the product, except when the local regulatory authority specifically requires a modification (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2C(R2) Guideline)15. It is a subset of information contained within the marketing authorisation holder’s reference product information for the periodic benefit-risk evaluation report. Where the reference product information is the company core data sheet, the reference safety information is the company core safety information
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Quote carries a footnote marker ('15') and is summarised.

f.title: Definition: serious adverse reaction
f.statement: Definition: a serious adverse reaction is one which results in death, is life-threatening, requires in-patient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect.

rows.quote: An adverse reaction which results in death, is life-threatening, requires in-patient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect [DIR 2001/83/EC Art 1(12)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Legal definition (DIR Art 1(12)) quoted exactly.

f.title: Apply medical judgement to important medical events; treat infectious agent transmission as serious
f.statement: Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether other situations, such as important medical events that might jeopardise the patient or require intervention, should be considered serious. Any suspected transmission via a medicinal product of an infectious agent is also considered a serious adverse reaction.

rows.quote: Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether other situations should be considered serious, such as important medical events that might not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but might jeopardise the patient or might require intervention to prevent one of the other outcomes listed in the definition above. Examples of such events are intensive treatment in an emergency room or at home for allergic bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias or convulsions that do not result in hospitalisation or development of dependency or abuse (see Annex GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D Guideline). Any suspected transmission via a medicinal product of an infectious agent is also considered a serious adverse reaction.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Recommended (should be exercised) correct; examples omitted from the statement; actor inferred.

f.title: Definition: signal; only adverse-reaction signals for EudraVigilance monitoring
f.statement: Definition: a signal is information from one or multiple sources suggesting a new potentially causal association, or a new aspect of a known association, between an intervention and an event or set of events, adverse or beneficial, judged of sufficient likelihood to justify verificatory action. For monitoring EudraVigilance data, only signals related to an adverse reaction shall be considered.

rows.quote: Information arising from one or multiple sources, including observations and experiments, which suggests a new potentially causal association, or a new aspect of a known association between an intervention and an event or set of related events, either adverse or beneficial, that is judged to be of sufficient likelihood to justify verificatory action [IR 520/2012 Art 19(1)]. New aspects of a known association may include changes in the frequency, distribution (e.g. gender, age and country), duration, severity or outcome of the adverse reaction. For the purpose of monitoring data in the EudraVigilance database, only signals related to an adverse reaction shall be considered [IR 520/2012 Art 19(1)].
rows.review_note: Review: Level Mandatory confirmed (IR 520/2012 Art 19(1) cited). Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Definition plus the 'shall be considered' clause from IR 520/2012 Art 19(1); 'new aspects' examples omitted.

f.title: Definition: solicited sources of ICSRs; treat solicited reports as study reports with causality assessment
f.statement: For the purpose of safety reporting, solicited reports should not be considered spontaneous but classified as individual case safety reports from studies, and therefore should have an appropriate causality assessment by a healthcare professional or the marketing authorisation holder.
f.clause: Annex I - Solicited sources of individual case safety reports

rows.quote: For the purpose of safety reporting, solicited reports should not be considered spontaneous but classified as individual case safety reports from studies and therefore should have an appropriate causality assessment by a healthcare professional or the marketing authorisation holder (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D).
rows.location: Annex I - Solicited sources of individual case safety reports
rows.review_note: Review: added missed requirement. Definition changes how reports are classified (solicited = study reports needing causality assessment); "should" -> Recommended, no legal citation. Double-check: Statement trimmed to the quote (the list of solicited data collection systems is not in the quote). Recommended (should) correct; quote names MAH or HCP for causality only.

f.title: Definition: spontaneous report, including stimulated reporting
f.statement: Definition: a spontaneous report is an unsolicited communication by a healthcare professional or consumer describing one or more adverse reactions in a patient given one or more medicinal products, not deriving from a study or organised data collection scheme. Reports stimulated by a DHPC, press publication or questioning by company representatives are considered spontaneous reports.

rows.quote: An unsolicited communication by a healthcare professional or consumer to a company, regulatory authority or other organisation (e.g. the World Health Organization, a regional centre, a poison control centre) that describes one or more adverse reactions in a patient who was given one or more medicinal products and that does not derive from a study or any organised data collection scheme (see GVP Annex IV, ICH-E2D). In this context, an adverse reaction refers to a suspected adverse reaction. Stimulated reporting can occur in certain situations, such as after a direct healthcare professional communication (DHPC), a publication in the press or questioning of healthcare professionals by company representatives, and adverse reaction reports arising from these situations are considered spontaneous reports
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Stimulated-reporting convention included; Recommended correct.

f.title: Definition: unexpected adverse reaction
f.statement: Definition: an unexpected adverse reaction is an adverse reaction the nature, severity or outcome of which is not consistent with the summary of product characteristics.

rows.quote: An adverse reaction, the nature, severity or outcome of which is not consistent with the summary of product characteristics [DIR 2001/83/EC Art 1(13)]
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Legal definition (DIR Art 1(13)) quoted exactly.

f.title: Definition: unexpected serious adverse reaction in a clinical trial
f.statement: Definition: in a clinical trial, an unexpected serious adverse reaction is a serious adverse reaction the nature, severity or outcome of which is not consistent with the reference safety information.

rows.quote: In the context of a clinical trial, an unexpected serious adverse reaction means a serious adverse reaction, the nature, severity or outcome of which is not consistent with the reference safety information [Reg (EU) No 536/2014 Art 2(2)(34)]
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). CTR definition from a footnote (Reg 536/2014 Art 2(2)(34)); sponsor actor inferred.

f.title: Expectedness: class reactions and which SmPC is the reference
f.statement: Unexpected adverse reactions include class-related reactions mentioned in the SmPC but not specifically described as occurring with the product. The relevant SmPC is that authorised by the competent authority of the Member State to which the reaction is reported (nationally authorised products), the SmPC authorised by the European Commission (centrally authorised products), or, between a favourable CHMP opinion and the Commission decision, the SmPC annexed to the CHMP opinion.

rows.quote: This includes class-related reactions which are mentioned in the summary of product characteristics (SmPC) but which are not specifically described as occurring with this product. For products authorised nationally, the relevant SmPC is that authorised by the competent authority in the Member State to whom the reaction is being reported. For centrally authorised products, the relevant SmPC is the SmPC authorised by the European Commission. During the time period between a CHMP opinion in favour of granting a marketing authorisation and the Commission decision granting the marketing authorisation, the relevant SmPC is the SmPC annexed to the CHMP opinion.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party). Relevant-SmPC rules paraphrased faithfully; no modal - level Recommended is a judgement call.

f.title: Definition: validated signal justifying further analysis
f.statement: Definition: a validated signal is a signal for which the signal validation process has verified that the available documentation contains sufficient evidence demonstrating a new potentially causal association, or a new aspect of a known association, and therefore justifies further analysis.

rows.quote: A signal for which the signal validation process has verified that the available documentation contains sufficient evidence demonstrating the existence of a new potentially causal association, or a new aspect of a known association, and therefore justifies further analysis of the signal.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Definition row: no modal verb or actor in the quote (term taken from the heading; actor inferred as the reporting party).
